title: Microsoft Teams: tenant meeting policy for who can start recording and transcription
summary: The briefing passes: its planned policy, default behaviour and rollout dates are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft's supplied notice, and the existing controls are documented. The sensitivity-label path needs one intervening wizard-page heading, a minor correction.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Teams meeting policy controlling who can start recording.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription, helping organizations apply consistent meeting settings.

claims.claim: The planned policy also controls who can start transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: The announced path is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Who can record and transcribe.
claims.quote: A new Who can record and transcribe policy control will be available in the Recording & transcription section of the applicable Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The new control is a single dropdown with four participant-scope and organiser-override combinations.
claims.quote: Administrators can select one of the following four options in a single dropdown:

claims.claim: The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change.
claims.quote: The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change, which preserves the current behavior.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk

claims.quote: No action is required. If you do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behavior remains unchanged.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says no action is required.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the new tenant policy at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '579860 Who can record policy' and 'Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy WhoCanRecordAndTranscribe tenant policy'; opened meeting-recording, manage-meeting-recording-options, meeting-templates-sensitivity-labels-policies and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. No new tenant role-selection policy was documented.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn documents the existing organiser choice between organisers and co-organisers or organisers, co-organisers and presenters.
claims.quote: Organizers with a Teams Premium license have two options for who can record and transcribe a meeting: Organizers and co-organizers; Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. The meeting organizer normally makes this choice when they create the meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Meeting templates can enforce who can record and transcribe in meetings using the template.
claims.quote: To restrict recording to organizers in meetings with sensitive information, use a meeting template or sensitivity label to enforce this setting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; controls[4].governs
claims.claim: Sensitivity labels can enforce who can record and transcribe in meetings carrying the label.
claims.quote: Meeting settings that you can apply with a sensitivity label: Who can record and transcribe

claims.claim: Learn currently states that there is no admin policy for Who can record.
claims.quote: Meeting recording can be disabled completely using a meeting policy, but there's no admin policy for Who can record.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Private-meeting recordings are uploaded to the meeting organiser's OneDrive.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Channel-meeting recordings are uploaded to SharePoint.
claims.quote: It gets uploaded to the meeting organizer's OneDrive (private meetings) or SharePoint (channel meetings).

claims.claim: Both the organiser and recording initiator need recording permissions under the existing recording policy.
claims.quote: Both the organizer and recording initiator need to have recording permissions to record the meeting or event.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes permission to start recording and transcription, not autonomous recording or transcription.
claims.quote: Teams administrators can use meeting policies to control who can start recording and transcription

claims.claim: Learn says recording and transcription are turned off when organisers turn off Copilot in Teams meetings and events.
claims.quote: When organizers turn off Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are also turned off.

claims.claim: The new policy remains subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and sensitivity labels configuring this option.
claims.quote: These configurations remain subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and any sensitivity label that configures this option.

claims.claim: The included licensing model represents a new policy option inside the Teams product, whose general licence requirement is named.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license. Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users in the organisation need a Teams licence to use Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Joining Teams meetings anonymously is an exception to that Teams licence requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The existing recording control is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting recording.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Turn the Meeting recording toggle On or Off.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCloudRecording $true enables recording for users with that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowCloudRecording $true

claims.where: controls[2].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The existing transcription control is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.where: controls[2].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true enables transcription for users with that meeting policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription is a per-organiser policy setting, requiring the organiser to have it enabled.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: Transcription is also a per-user policy setting, requiring the initiating user to have it enabled.
claims.quote: The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: The template control is Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting templates > Add > Recording & transcription > Who can record.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and select Meeting templates. Select Add. ... Recording & transcription ... Who can record

claims.claim: No setter is documented for the template's Who can record setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams meeting template Who can record PowerShell Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration setter'; opened create-custom-meeting-template and Get-CsTeamsMeetingTemplateConfiguration. The documented configuration is read only; no operation setting the option was found.

claims.claim: A meeting template can lock the recording-role option or let the organiser change it.
claims.quote: Who can record ... Setting can be enforced or meeting organizer can be allowed to change.

claims.claim: The Purview label path reaches Control who can record and transcribe through the label scope and Protect Teams meetings and chats selection.
claims.quote: On the Settings for Teams meetings and chats page, choose the following values: ... Select Control who can record and transcribe and choose Organizers and co-organizers from the dropdown list.
claims.fix: In controls[4].ui.path and the rendered table, use 'Solutions > Information protection > Labels > Create a label > Define the scope for this label > Choose protection settings for types of items you selected > Protect Teams meetings and chats > Settings for Teams meetings and chats > Control who can record and transcribe'. The missing step is the intervening wizard-page heading documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/configure-meetings-sensitive-protection.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label name> -TeamsWhoCanRecord <value> is the documented sensitivity-label setter for the recording-role option.
claims.quote: Use the Set-Label cmdlet to modify sensitivity labels in your organization. [-Identity] <ComplianceRuleIdParameter> ... [-TeamsWhoCanRecord <Microsoft.Office.CompliancePolicy.PolicyConfiguration.WhoCanRecordOptions>]

claims.claim: The label procedure selects Files & other data assets, Emails and Meetings in scope before protecting Teams meetings and chats.
claims.quote: On the Define the scope for this label page, make sure Files & other data assets, Emails, and Meetings are selected.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label's Who can record and transcribe option does not take effect in Meet Now meetings.
claims.quote: The following meeting options won't take effect for a Meet Now meeting: Who can record and transcribe

claims.claim: Preventing meetings and events from being recorded entirely requires recording policies in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: If you need to prevent meetings and events from being recorded entirely, you must use the recording policies in the Teams admin center. This setting applies to the people or groups that you specify, but can't be applied through a meeting template or sensitivity label.
